claim: Scouting pass, no theorem activated. A symmetric three-place law can fail on plain cubic systems only if it excludes both constant colourings (W within {1, 2}); among the seven symmetric knots only not-all-equal does, so on plain systems no other knot has unsolvable spaces at all. Exactly-one (and exactly-two) can fail, but deciding them on cubic systems is NP-complete (exact cover by 3-sets with every element in three sets, Gonzalez 1985; the dual correspondence checked on 120 systems), so their failures are coNP-complete to recognise. Interest 0/3 as a standalone epic.
conclusion: Plain systems: mutual selection is special to the knot (only not-all-equal can fail recognisably).
